task: Physical energy perturbations, odd hidden states, and exact intervention-information obstruction
scope: An exact model-class obstruction, not a physical implementation or an empirical acquisition. The clock perturbation and its FDT are classical; the application is closure of the accepted parity-completion interface under arbitrary observable clock policies.

sources.title: On a Response Formula and Its Interpretation
sources.passages: Equations (7)–(10), (20), and the b=0,a=beta paragraph immediately following equation (20)
sources.bearing: Exact antecedent: departure-rate energy perturbation, all-orders stationary Gibbs reweighting, equilibrium-form response for an irreversible baseline. Also kinetic freedom at fixed energy-ratio change.

sources.title: Markovian perturbation, response and fluctuation dissipation theorem
sources.version_read: Published Annales de l'Institut Henri Poincare, Probabilites et Statistiques 46, 822–852; earlier arXiv:0710.4394v2 also inspected
sources.passages: Introduction, Theorem 2.10 with proof, Proposition 3.1 and its time-change construction, and statement of Proposition 5.1
sources.bearing: Strongest general invariant-measure FDT and time-change comparator; no symmetry of the baseline semigroup is required for the stated FDT identity.

sources.authors: Marco Baiesi, Eliran Boksenbojm, Christian Maes and Bram Wynants
sources.title: Nonequilibrium Linear Response for Markov Dynamics, II: Inertial Dynamics
sources.passages: Introduction, physical momentum reversal, section 3 equation (10), and the entropic/frenetic response discussion
sources.bearing: An actual potential perturbation acts as a specified force in the momentum equation; physical odd-variable response requires more than a generic energy label or an all-even rate tilt.

sources.title: Energy dissipation and violation of the fluctuation-response relation in nonequilibrium Langevin systems
sources.version_read: arXiv:cond-mat/0510723v1, 2005-10-27; publication metadata verified against Physical Review E
sources.passages: Introduction including assumptions (A1) and (A2); equation (5); beginning of section II, equations (6)–(7); statements covering inertial and overdamped cases
sources.bearing: Strongest quantitative comparator under a known Langevin bath/force contract: equality for dissipated power from fluctuations and force response, including inertia. Not a generic hidden-state theorem.

sources.authors: Eugenia Franco, Bernhard Kepka and Juan J. L. Velazquez
sources.title: Characterizing the Detailed Balance Property by Means of Measurements
sources.version_read: Published Archive for Rational Mechanics and Analysis 250, article 25, 2026-04-03

sources.bearing: Ordinary detailed-balance criterion from reciprocal propagator measurements with graph and robustness hypotheses. Its admissible microscopic rate class is not acquired by observing a few coarse energy-control directions.

corrections_and_boundaries: Canonical stationary reweighting and equilibrium-form FDT do not by themselves imply detailed balance.
The symmetric exponential edge tilt need not be equilibrium-compatible for odd hidden variables.
The exact control closure requires potentials determined by the observed state label and controls whose only kinetic effect is the stated row-wise clock factor.
A fully specified mechanical or Hamiltonian perturbation may exclude this rate family; no physical realization is asserted.
A quantitative bound from response discrepancy needs kinetic sensitivity or another physical scale; the saved three-cycle example holds its discrepancy fixed while entropy tends to zero.
The arbitrary-protocol theorem is a proof consequence, not an empirical conclusion from finitely many matrix checks.
